cohort: 1009 pregnant women screened for SARS-CoV-2 infection at admission to the delivery ward in 45 hospitals across Spain
finding: Pregnant women infected with SARS-CoV-2 had a higher risk of preterm birth, premature rupture of membranes at term, and neonatal intensive care unit admissions compared to uninfected pregnant women.
mod_finding: Iatrogenic preterm delivery was more frequent in infected women, while the occurrence of spontaneous preterm deliveries was statistically similar between infected and uninfected women.
